items.title: Codex CLI 0.171.0 makes GPT-6.2 Sol default and enables TUI workspace
facts: Added GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra to model catalogs, with Sol as the default catalog selection.
Enabled the TUI workspace by default, with searchable document previews, image previews, and subagent transcripts alongside the main conversation.
Added codex exec --remote <ADDR> to start or resume noninteractive sessions on an existing app server.

items.title: Claude Code 2.1.329 adds hook trust warnings and expands /tasks view
facts: Added a trust dialog warning that says where a folder's hooks are declared.
Added this session's scheduled tasks, /loop wakeups, the goal and this conversation's forks to /tasks; x stops one after asking.
Added a warning in the conversation, in Claude Desktop and other non-interactive hosts, when hooks in managed settings fail to load.

items.title: Stripe Evals shows coding agents average 78% but only 29% strict pass on payment tasks
facts: We ran 69 scenarios across one-time payments, subscriptions, and Connect on 14 model and harness pairs, both with and without the Stripe agent plugin.
While the headline numbers are high, a strict pass rate requiring all necessary criteria to pass drops the average score across all agents from 78.1% to 29.4%.
All 14 coding agents scored higher with the plugin, by roughly 3 to 8 percentage points, and web searches fell 96%.

items.title: Kong launches Volcano self-healing agent cloud for coding agents
facts: Today we are announcing Volcano, a new self-healing agent cloud that provides in one place everything developers need to build agents and applications at scale.
Volcano hosts all applications, agents, data storage and other capabilities that can be used seamlessly from your favorite coding harness (Cursor, Codex, Claude Code, and more).
Once your agents, backends and frontends are running in Volcano, Volcano kicks in and works for you to continuously identify issues and provide resolutions to bugs.

items.title: Microsoft unveils MAI Code 2 coding models at Ignite 2026
facts: Microsoft AI introduced MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash, the second generation of its coding model line.

Averaged across four benchmarks, Microsoft says MAI Code 2 delivers about 98% of OpenAI GPT-6.1 Sol’s performance at roughly 40% of the price, and about 96% of Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5’s performance at roughly 5% of the price.
Both are available now in GitHub Copilot.

items.title: Matt Pocock viral prompt treats code comments as harmful for AI agents
facts: Take a look at every code comment in my codebase. Categorise each comment as: Tautology, Excuse, Stale, or Decision Record.
For each comment, take this action: Tautology/Stale: delete the comment; Excuse: delete the comment and file an issue; Decision Record: move it into an ADR.
I'm sold - comments considered harmful.

items.title: GrokBot engineer explains formal verification risks when AI writes code and specs
facts: GrokBot engineer Lauren Tan: 'You could be proving false is true' she explained formal verification in 60 seconds.
the trap is drift. the proof lives in a different language than your code. so how do you know the model you proved actually matches what runs in production?
if no human reads the spec, the machine can guarantee your code follows some intent. 'But is that intent correct?'

items.title: Apple job listing describes AI agent that browses, codes, and drives apps
facts: Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does.
It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step.
The agents can also coordinate specialized sub-agents along the way.

items.title: Developer benchmarks Gemini Carbon 4 as strong orchestrator in Antigravity
facts: Ladies and Gents, Gemini Carbon 4 on noahbench! This model places FIRST when it comes to mechanics.
Carbon is fable class model... implementation is a solved problem.
Overall, Carbon is an absurdly knowledgeable model that performs very well in a knowledge focused position such as an orchestrator.
